blockNote: Shadow's Aura body sprites (Bank 17, 1556480-1557571 = $17:C000): 3 animations, 55 frame records, 23 sprite groups, 80 sub-sprites. This is the spriteset of body_table row $08 (art shad_sprites_1BC000, the same tile graphics as Shadow's normal body, spriteset_shadow). Nothing else selects the row: PlayerAuraTransformEntry (player_transition_handlers, entered from item_use_system.UseItem_Aura when Shadow uses the Aura item standing still) calls SetPlayerSpriteDirect #08. The item's own description string is 'Dark Knight Shadow's Body turns to water' (item_description_table $24), which is what these frames show. The old note ('Shadow's unique movement and combat modes') named no code, and the body_table note said that nothing selects row $08; both were wrong.
The struct format (table, frame list, group header, sub-sprite) is described once, in the spriteset_freedan block note.

| $00 | 20 (holds $13, 5, 5, 4, 4, 3, then 13 x 2, then 0) | PlayerAuraTransformEntry: StageSpriteFrame #00 + AnimOnce, first thing after SetPlayerSpriteDirect #08 | 6 groups of 6, 6, 4, 4, 2 and 4 sub-sprites, then 13 groups of 1-7 sub-sprites, then the one-sprite group 17C42F |

| $01 | 19 | PlayerAuraBlockedBySolid (the abort path): StageSpriteFrame #01 + AnimOnce at the original spot, then exit | The same groups as $00 in reverse order (13 small groups, then the 6 large ones, last hold $13), without the final group 17C42F |

| $02 | 16, all hold 0 | PlayerAuraLandAnimLoop: StageSpriteMoveY #02, #01 (Y chain 1 = +1 px per frame) | Alternates the single-sprite groups 17C3DE / 17C3F2 and the four-sprite group 17C406 with the one-sprite group 17C42F every second frame |

The order of the calls is traced; what the frames look like on screen (a body that flattens, rises again, drips) is only read off the shapes: the shrinking sub-sprite counts of $00 and their reversal in $01 match 'turns to water' and the abort that shows the body again, but the art was not viewed (OQ-I071-1). The palette the frames use and where the Aura sequence ends (PlayerAuraTransformExit) are not covered here.

1091 bytes = 6 (3 pointers) + 3 x 2 (list terminators) + 55 x 4 (records) + 23 x 13 (group headers) + 80 x 7 (sub-sprites). All 23 groups are referenced by the three lists; groups 17C0E8 to 17C1C3 are the six large ones, 17C3DE / 17C3F2 / 17C406 / 17C42F are only used by $02 (17C42F also ends $00).

spriteset_shadow_mode: Animation table of the Aura body (body_table row $08), 3 pointers: $00 = the body turning to water (played once), $01 = the same groups in reverse (the abort path), $02 = 16 one-tick frames played while the player sinks (Y +1 px per frame). The caller of all three is player_transition_handlers.PlayerAuraTransformEntry.
sprite_set_17C006: Animation $00, 20 records: the large body group 17C0E8 for 20 ticks, five shrinking groups (holds 5, 5, 4, 4, 3), thirteen small groups of 2 ticks each, and the closing one-sprite group 17C42F.
sprite_set_17C058: Animation $01, 19 records: the groups of $00 in reverse order, from the smallest (17C1EC) back to the large body group 17C0E8 (last hold $13). Shown by the abort branch of the Aura sequence.
sprite_set_17C0A6: Animation $02, 16 records, all hold 0: the groups 17C3DE, 17C406, 17C3F2 and 17C406 (two records each) alternate with the one-sprite group 17C42F. Staged with Y chain 1 while the player sinks.
sprite_group_17C0E8: The large body group: 6 sub-sprites, first record of $00 and last of $01.
sprite_group_17C42F: One sub-sprite (tile word $041E, offsets 0,0): the closing record of $00 and every second frame of $02.

blockNote: Treasure chest placement (Bank 01, 109992-110726 = $01:ADA8): a pointer table of 255 words (scene ID $00-$FE) followed by the chest lists. Only 39 scenes have chests, in 46 records; the other 216 entries point at one shared empty list (chest_entry_01AFA6, a single $FF byte). The old note ('barrier/chest placement', 'event-blocking barrier tiles', bit 7 as an end sentinel in the flag byte) was wrong: the table holds chests only, and the terminator is a byte >= $80 in the first (X) byte of a record.
=== RECORD (4 bytes, extraction: chest-entry < X, Y, contents, flag >) ===
| +0 | X tile of the chest's left column. A value with bit 7 set ends the list ($FF in every list) |
| +1 | Y tile of the chest's BOTTOM row (the top row is Y-1) |
| +2 | Contents: the item ID given by GiveItemToPlayer (names in system_strings.item_name_table); 0 = flag-only chest (shows 'It is empty!') |

| +3 | Bits 0-6: event flag ($0200 group, TestEventFlag_0200 / SetEventFlag_0200) set when the chest is opened; bit 7: open with the fanfare (ChestOpeningActor with the music transition) instead of the plain 'found' dialogue |
A chest is 2x2 map tiles: closed $FA/$FB (top row) and $F8/$F9 (bottom row), open $FE/$FF and $FC/$FD. The list is chosen by the scene index $0646 (scene x 2) into the pointer table.
- PlaceOpenedChestTiles (warps_interaction): at scene build, every record whose flag is set is drawn open.

- HandleChestInteraction (warps_interaction, via CheckWarpAndChest): matches the chest tile in front of the player against bytes +0 / +1, then DrawChestTiles and GiveItemToPlayer. A chest tile with no record shows 'The jewel box is tightly closed.'
- radar_map_screen: one icon for every chest whose flag is still clear.
=== CONTENT (all 46 records; item numbers as in item_name_table) ===
| Scene | Records < X, Y -> contents, flag > (F = fanfare) |
| $4D | 39,31 -> Crystal Ball, $0A F; 09,33 -> Herb, $0B; 34,05 -> Red Jewel, $0C |

Counts: 44 item chests (21 Red Jewel, 10 Herb, 4 Crystal Ball, 3 Mushroom Drop, 2 Rama Statue, and one each of Blue Block, Mystic Statue, Magic Dust, Teapot) and 2 flag-only chests (scenes $60 and $61). The 13 records with the fanfare bit are exactly the chests that hold something other than a Herb or a Red Jewel. Each flag $01-$2E is used once; $2E is the flag-only chest of scene $60, out of sequence.
Byte check: 734 = 255 x 2 (pointers) + 1 (the shared empty list) + 46 x 4 (records) + 39 (one $FF per non-empty list). The extraction does not print the $FF terminators.

scene_chest_table: Pointer table: 255 words, index = scene ID ($00-$FE; scene $FF has no entry). 216 entries point at chest_entry_01AFA6; 39 scenes point at their own list.
chest_entry_01AFA6: The shared empty list (just the $FF terminator), used by every scene without a chest.
chest_entry_01AFA7: First non-empty list: scene $0E, one Herb chest (flag $01).
chest_entry_01AFC9: Scene $2E: the Mystic Statue chest (item $38, flag $08, fanfare).
chest_entry_01AFD3: Scene $4D: the only list with 3 chests (Crystal Ball with fanfare, Herb, Red Jewel).
chest_entry_01B010: Scene $60: the first record is a flag-only chest (contents 0, flag $2E, the only flag out of sequence), the second a Rama Statue chest (flag $17, fanfare).
chest_entry_01B019: Scene $61: a single flag-only chest (contents 0, flag $18); it shows 'It is empty!' and sets its flag.

blockNote: Sprite sets of the inventory screen (Bank 10, 1081344-1085191 = $10:8000): 77 animations ($00-$4C), 150 frame records, 129 labelled sprite groups with 181 sub-sprites as the extraction prints them, plus 5 unlabelled groups that the extraction hides inside two of the labelled ones (see the last section). The inventory actors select it with SetMetasprite @inventory_spritemap (InventoryMenuInit, inventory_statue_slot) and their animation index $28 picks the pointer. The struct format (table, frame list, group header, sub-sprite) is described once, in the spriteset_freedan block note. The old note ('OAM layouts for item icons, cursor sprites, tab indicators and equipment display') names tab indicators, but no index is left for them: the indices are accounted for below except $41-$43.

| $00-$3F | Item icons: the animation index of an InventorySlotActor is the item ID stored in its slot ($28 = 0 hides the actor), and EquippedItemDisplay uses inventoryEquippedType. The sets for the blank IDs $29-$36 are single static frames; $37, $38 and $39 share one group (108ACC) |
| $3A-$3F | The six mystic-statue pedestal icons: inventory_statue_slot copies byte +1 of its statue_reward_table row to $28. By the item-ID rule they are also the icons of items $3A-$3F |
| $40 | The selection / equip cursor (SelectionCursorActor: StageSprAndHitbox #40). $41, $42 and $43 point to the same group (108BAA); no code was found that selects them |

| $44-$4C | The three status-row sprites at X $98: StatusAbilityRow0 / 1 / 2 (top, middle, bottom row) stage characterForm x 3 + $44 / $45 / $46. The code comments call them portraits. Form 0 uses $44-$46, form 1 $47-$49, form 2 $4A-$4C |
Most sets are one static frame (hold 0). The animated ones are the item icons $01, $05, $08, $09, $0D, $10, $12 (7 frames), $1C (13 frames) and $24, and the status-row sets $44-$4C (4-9 frames).

Only groups that a frame list points at get a label. The group at 108B67 (used by $3F) is followed by 2 groups that no list references, and the group at 108BAA (used by $40-$43) by 3 more. The extraction cannot tell where a group ends, so it prints each labelled group with every following byte as extra sub-sprites: 108B67 shows 8 sub-sprites for a region of 67 bytes (13 + 54) and 108BAA shows 10 for 80 bytes, and each listing is 2 and 3 bytes longer than the data. Reading the two regions as headers plus sub-sprites gives 3 groups (13 x 3 + 4 x 7 = 67) and 4 groups (13 x 4 + 4 x 7 = 80). The sub-sprites printed after the first 1-2 real ones in those two groups are therefore not sub-sprites of that group (proposal R-I071-3).

3847 bytes = 154 (77 pointers) + 77 x 2 + 150 x 4 (list terminators and records) + 129 x 13 (labelled group headers) + 181 x 7 (printed sub-sprites) - 5 (the listing overrun of the two groups above). The first set starts at 10809A, directly after the table. File read sampled (~45%): the table, the sets of $00-$4C, the first and last groups and the two long groups; the per-group art was not compared with the item names.

inventory_spritemap: 77 pointers, animation index = item ID for $00-$3F (see the block note for $3A-$3F, the cursor $40 and the status rows $44-$4C). Most targets are a single static frame.
sprite_set_1082B6: Animation $40: the selection cursor (SelectionCursorActor). $41, $42 and $43 point at the same group, 108BAA.
sprite_set_1082CE: Animation $44: the first of the nine status-row sets (5 frames; $44 + characterForm x 3 + the row: 0 top, 1 middle, 2 bottom).
sprite_group_108B67: Statue icon of animation $3F, followed by 2 unreferenced groups: the sub-sprites printed below the first ones are the headers and sub-sprites of those groups (67 bytes in all).
sprite_group_108BAA: The cursor group of animations $40-$43, followed by 3 unreferenced groups: only the first sub-sprites printed are its own (80 bytes in all).
